ai.title: Remove outdated knowledge.md sections
ai.summary: Deleted obsolete documentation from knowledge.md, including legacy file change strategies, project templates, referral system details, and duplicated backward compatibility guidelines. Replaced specific Claude/Mani references with generic LLM integration notes. Updated main components list to reflect current architecture. Scope limited to internal repo documentation.

eli5.text: Some of the instructions you see when working inside the Codebuff project have been cleaned up. They removed a bunch of old documentation about how parts of the software used to work, like how files were changed, what starter templates looked like, and how a referral program worked. They also replaced specific references to the old assistant name with more general language. You wouldn't notice this unless you were looking at the project's internal guides and documentation.

ai.title: Update thinking-stream prompt to avoid angle brackets in tool
ai.summary: Updated thinking-stream.ts guidelines to instruct the model to refer to tool calls without angle brackets (e.g., "use the end_turn tool" instead of "<end_turn>"). This prevents the model from accidentally generating literal tags inside the thinking block, which could interfere with stream parsing. The change applies to the backend thinking stream prompt guidelines.

eli5.text: When the assistant is thinking out loud before answering, it sometimes accidentally wrote its own instructions in between angle brackets like <end_turn>, which confused the system parsing its thoughts. The fix tells the assistant to talk about tools using plain words instead of angle brackets, so referring to the end_turn tool rather than <end_turn>. You wouldn't see this directly, but it helps prevent glitches in how the assistant's private thinking gets processed behind the scenes. It's a small behind-the-scenes tweak that only affects internal systems.

ai.title: Fix cd persistence prompt
ai.summary: Updated backend/src/tools.ts to state cwd is persistent. Removed incorrect instructions claiming cwd resets per command and requiring cd subdir && cmd chaining. Aligns tool guidance with actual shell session behavior.

eli5.text: The assistant's built-in guidance about how changing folders works has been corrected. Previously, it was told that each command starts in your original folder, meaning actions like cd wouldn't stick between commands unless chained with &&. Now, the guidance reflects that folder changes actually persist across commands in the same session. This affects anyone watching how the assistant plans which commands to run, since the model no longer expects directories to reset unexpectedly. The corrected prompt is live today, and nothing about how you interact with the assistant changes, only how it internally reasons about file locations.

ai.title: Add referencedby metadata to readfiles tool results
ai.summary: read_files tool results now include a <referenced_by> field listing files that call tokens defined in the read file. Mechanism: getFileTokenScores builds a tokenCallers map during code-map parsing, passed to renderReadFilesResult in backend prompts. Scope: packages/code-map (parse.ts, languages.ts, tree-sitter queries), backend/src/util/parse-tool-call-xml.ts, npm-app context workers. Detail: MAX_CALLERS limits caller lists to 25 files per token to control context size.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads a file as part of understanding your project, that file's summary now includes a new section listing which other files reference or call the key names defined in it, capped at 25 entries per name to avoid bloating the conversation. This appears in the project analysis views that shape what the assistant knows about your codebase, so you'll notice richer context when the assistant discusses how files relate to each other. The feature is live today as part of the project context that's assembled when the assistant loads your project.

ai.title: code-map: skip default object properties
ai.summary: code-map parse.ts adds filter for default object properties. Token names like toString, hasOwnProperty now skipped via in {} check. Prevents false positives in getFileTokenScores. Internal fix, no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The code analysis tool now correctly ignores common built-in object names like 'toString' or 'hasOwnProperty' when scanning your projects, so those standard terms won't trigger false warnings anymore. This only affects how the internal analysis engine processes code, and there's nothing you'd see differently in your day-to-day usage since it was producing inaccurate data behind the scenes before.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.267
ai.summary: Package version incremented from 1.0.266 to 1.0.267 in `npm-app/package.json`. Routine release update.

eli5.text: You, as someone running the assistant, just pulled in a new release that includes a small fix: when the assistant maps out a project's structure, it now skips over default placeholder values in object definitions, so its view of your code stays cleaner. This release also brings the latest housekeeping updates like refreshed documentation, tweaked prompts, and improved file-reference metadata. The packaging change itself only updated the version label and is live today.

ai.title: CLI class switched to singleton pattern
ai.summary: CLI class in npm-app/src/cli.ts now uses a private constructor with static initialize and getInstance methods. npm-app/src/index.ts calls CLI.initialize then CLI.getInstance instead of new CLI. Prevents multiple CLI instances and throws on double-init or pre-init access.

eli5.text: The team tightened up how the command-line version of their assistant starts up, so it can only be turned on once per session instead of accidentally creating multiple copies of itself. If someone tries to start it twice or grab an instance before it's ready, the system now throws an error instead of silently misbehaving. This is purely internal housekeeping; you won't see any visible difference in day-to-day use.

ai.title: Terminal timeout handling supports null and snakecase rename
ai.summary: runTerminalCommand in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts now accepts negative timeoutSeconds as null to disable timeouts. Internal PTY and child process runners conditionally create timers and guard clearTimeout calls. Scope limited to npm-app terminal utilities.

eli5.text: If you run a command in the terminal and give it a negative timeout, the system now treats that as "no timeout" instead of misbehaving. When there's no timeout set, the program skips setting up the countdown timer entirely and guards against trying to clear a timer that was never created. This applies to the internal terminal utilities and is live today for anyone running commands through that module.

ai.title: Update working directory prompts and simplify terminal cwd output
ai.summary: Moved working directory guidance from global `toolsInstructions` to `run_terminal_command` description in `backend/src/tools.ts`. Removed critical block stating relative filepaths always start from project root, adding explicit warning to check cwd before execution. `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` simplified `cwdMessage` logic to always report final cwd, removing conditional empty string when unchanged. Minor syntax cleanup removing trailing semicolons on variable declarations.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the assistant will now always tell you what directory it ended up in, even if it didn't change. Previously, it would stay quiet when the directory hadn't moved. The reminder to check your current directory before running commands was moved to a more visible spot, so you won't accidentally run something in the wrong place.
